item.title: Get into national parks free on Feb. 16 — but there’s a catch
item.description: Parks will be free to enter for U.S. legal residents only.

item.title: David Gardner: Your tax refund may be bigger than expected
item.description: With most of your tax documents likely in hand, it’s time to think about when to file your 2025 return. This year more than most it makes sense to explore filing as soon as possible, as refunds are expected to be larger than average.

item.title: Niwot’s Hunter Robbie named Colorado’s XC Gatorade Player of the Year
item.description: His team from this past fall season will go down in history as one of the best ever at the high school level, as the Cougars set record-low scores in runaway wins at the Class 5A state meet and Nike Cross Nationals.

item.title: Aggressive CU Buffs rout BYU in women’s basketball
item.description: There were plenty of numbers Saturday that were impressive for the Colorado women’s basketball team. What might have impressed head coach JR Payne the most, however, was the number of times her players dove to the floor or fought for rebounds during a 76-46 rout of BYU at the CU Events Center.

item.title: Mead’s Liam Kelly, Carter Woods win 4A Region 2 wrestling titles
item.description: After Mead’s Liam Kelly wrapped up his 165-lb. finals win over Niwot's Eli Quesada, a wrestler from another school asked him what grade he was in.

item.title: No. 22 BYU turns away Colorado’s upset bid
item.description: Brigham Young immortalized a program all-timer by retiring the No. 32 jersey of former Cougars sharpshooter Jimmer Fredette. Colorado shook off its recent road doldrums and did its best to ruin the party.

item.title: Colorado answers the call despite OT loss at No. 22 BYU
item.description: There was no sudden moment of clarity. No spark of inspiration in the form of the proverbial light bulb brightening overhead.

item.title: CSU Rams rally past Wyoming in final minutes to claim home Border War victory
item.description: With the win, the Rams improved to 15-10 overall and 6-8 in the Mountain West Conference

item.title: Holy Family’s Lorelai Frauenfelder wins two more state titles at 3A swim meet
item.description: A day after Broomfield High School ran away with the Class 4A state title at Veterans Memorial Aquatic Center, Holy Family — the private school from down the road — celebrated a banner day from its senior star, Lorelai Frauenfelder.

item.title: Front Range regional wrestling recap: 66 locals headed to the state tournament
item.description: BoCoPreps teams qualified 51 boys and 15 girls for next week’s state wrestling tournament. The championships will be held at Ball Arena, running Thursday-Saturday. Punching their ticket there on Saturday, Broomfield’s boys led with an area-most eight state qualifiers. Individuals had to place in the top four of their regional weight class to advance to Ball Arena. Meanwhile, Holy Family got seven through from both its boys and girls teams.
